reasoning_traces.think:
The runtime infrastructure enforces a strict separation between client and server execution environments. In SSR, all rendering happens on the server, preventing direct access to browser APIs like window or localStorage. This ensures deterministic behavior and security by design. Server-only logic is encapsulated using TanStack Start's server functions, which execute exclusively on the backend. These functions handle authentication, data fetching, and mutations safely without exposing secrets or binding information to the frontend. The design inspector bridge operates within an iframe, maintaining isolation between the parent UI and child runtime components. It uses compile-time guards to prevent accidental injection of instrumentation code into the rendered DOM. The system avoids global mutable state in workers, relying instead on cryptographic randomness for unique identifiers. This architecture supports both robustness against side-channel attacks and scalability through stateless request processing.
